correctness.rationale: For all positive radii and every direction, direct normal-cone optimality proves the two exact support branches. An exhaustive 48-chamber spherical partition and monotone chamber-coordinate inversion give the one-quadrature CDF. Above the 2/sqrt(3) normalized support threshold the eight diagonal spherical caps are disjoint, implying the exact linear upper tail. The six axial logarithmic product-strip sublevel sets contribute 6/pi delta log(1/delta); remainder on smooth coordinate great-circle arcs is O(delta). The included independently constrained optimizer/quadrature/Sobol checker replayed 251 diagnostics; finite checks are not used to prove the formulas. No statement about arbitrary unequal cylinder intersections is made.

value.rationale: The classical Steinmetz tricylinder is a natural convex intersection with well-studied volume, surface, and central sections. Its full directional support and scalar width law are not routine substitutions of those measurements. The exact high-width uniform law and logarithmic lower tail show contrasting geometric singularities—eight vertex normal cones versus six transverse crossings of minimum-width great circles. These provide reproducible distributional invariants for integral geometry of a classical shape rather than an arbitrary slice or cosmetic numerical gain.
